newsitem.title: FRANCE: BoF exempts repo ops from reserve requirements.
newsitem.headline: BoF exempts repo ops from reserve requirements.

text.p: The Bank of France said on Thursday it had decided to exempt repo transactions from reserve requirements.

The move will translate for banks into an increase of around one billion francs in their liquidity, the Bank said. It eases by 13 percent the amount of deposits that the banks must constitute to satisfy reserve requirement rules, it said.
The move, it said, was aimed at taking into account "the development and maturity of the French repo market to assure access in fully harmonious conditions to all economic players".
The Bank stressed, however, that the move was strictly confined to repo operations and did not put into question the role that reserves can play in carrying out monetary policy.

The central bank said the decision was aimed at allowing the repo market to develop fully against a European backdrop in which it will be among one of the most important intervention tools of the European central bank system.
The Bank said the move was aimed at establishing a level playing field for repo transactions.

Until now, repo operations with a maturity equal to or below one year carried out with credit establishments by resident counterparties were subject to reserve requirements. The exception was when those counterparties were themselves the credit etablishments subject to the reserves.
This constituted a differentiating factor among the various market players which "seemed desirable to abolish", it said.
Now, with the exemption of reserves, "repo transactions will be conducted on a unified basis..."
"Access to the market by all financial institutions, whether or not credit establishments, will be helped," it said.
